# Who unrolls a constant loop, part two: the platform has a say as well as the
# language.
#
# html writes its view as markup -- a file in static mode, a string in a
# handler in route mode -- and the only iteration it can emit is over an
# expression that varies with the request. A `for` over a compile-time constant
# is not one, so nothing iterates it and the loop renders its body once with
# its variable bound to nothing. `sngl doc --http` lost its whole package list
# that way under --lang go: seven links became a single empty <a>.

sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o routed app.sngl
grep '/p/alpha[^>]*>alpha</a>' routed/server.go
grep '/p/beta[^>]*>beta</a>' routed/server.go
grep '/p/gamma[^>]*>gamma</a>' routed/server.go

# The iterations are the markup, so no loop is left for Go to run.
! grep 'range' routed/server.go

# Static mode is the same platform answering the same way.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o static app.sngl
grep '/p/alpha[^>]*>alpha</a>' static/index.html
grep '/p/gamma[^>]*>gamma</a>' static/index.html

# A constant loop that runs no iterations is dropped, whether or not it has an
# else to run instead. An expansion of nothing reads as an empty expansion, not
# as an iterable the optimizer could not evaluate -- which left an else-less
# loop standing, and one empty row rendered per empty list.
sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o empty empty.sngl
grep 'still here' empty/server.go
! grep 'class=[^>]*row' empty/server.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:app"
import "sngl:platform/html"

const packages list<string> = ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]

component main {
    window #home(title="Docs", href="/") {
        html.nav {
            for var p = packages {
                html.a(href="/p/" + p, innerText=p)
            }
        }
    }
}

-- empty.sngl --
import . "sngl:app"
import "sngl:platform/html"

const packages list<string> = []

component main {
    window #home(title="Docs", href="/") {
        html.nav {
            html.span(innerText="still here")
            for var p = packages {
                html.li(class="row", innerText=p)
            }
        }
    }
}
